claims.text: NiTi shape-memory alloys exhibit temperature-dependent plastic deformation behavior.
Phase transformations in NiTi modify dislocation dynamics and mobility.
Cold-worked NiTi is predominantly martensitic at lower temperatures.
Controlled heating can induce a martensite-to-austenite transformation in NiTi.
The relevant NiTi transformation temperature is around 30–40 °C.
The martensite-to-austenite transformation mediates the temperature dependence of deformation.
The phase transformation alters dislocation paths.
The phase transformation alters internal stress distributions.
These microstructural changes enhance ductility and permit more pronounced plastic deformation.
Above the transformation threshold, NiTi will show greater ductility and plastic deformation than at lower temperatures.
Above the transformation threshold, NiTi will show increased reversible shape change.
At room temperature, martensite is dominant and plastic deformation is more limited.
The deformation effect is most pronounced while the temperature spans approximately 30–40 °C and changes less outside that range.
Transition temperatures and deformation enhancement depend on composition, processing history, and experimental conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes enhanced plastic deformation but includes reversible shape change as that outcome. Plastic strain is ordinarily irreversible, whereas reversible NiTi shape change can arise from recoverable transformation strain; the fields do not distinguish these deformation modes.
